poster.title: Pedro Páramo
poster.bookOrigin: Mexican Spanish-language novel by Juan Rulfo, first published in Mexico City in 1955.
poster.creator: Ricardo Martínez (vignette)
poster.alt: A worn cream jacket with a fine double ruled frame, orange italic title, black author name, and a small dark vignette of an upright draped form among long curved points.
poster.blurb: A small, sharp vignette interrupts a quiet structure of rules and lettering.

notes.title: The displayed edition
notes.body: Fondo de Cultura Económica, Mexico City, 1955; Letras Mexicanas 19, first edition. The jacket photograph comes from Cristian Astete’s documented copy.

notes.title: Writing and image-making
notes.body: The Ricardo Martínez foundation documents his vignettes for the 1955 Pedro Páramo. This supports the illustration credit, without assigning every typographic or publishing element to him.

notes.title: A visible design relationship
notes.body: The orange title is echoed by the smaller series line. Thin rectangular rules contrast with the vignette’s curved and pointed shapes.

studyData.intro: A small vignette interrupts a restrained frame of rules and type. The whole printed vignette stays together: its thin points and interlocking figures are studied without forcing an uncertain cut through the illustration.

regions.label: An interlocking central vignette
regions.summary: A compact upright form sits among long pointed shapes in the lower middle of the jacket.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A compact upright form sits among long pointed shapes in the lower middle of the jacket. Dark outlines and lighter internal marks overlap within the small illustration.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The small image gains emphasis from the paper around it. Its interlocking contours resist an instant reading, inviting closer inspection after the title.

sections.heading: The artist’s foundation identifies the image
sections.body: The Ricardo Martínez foundation describes this cover vignette as two figures embracing with a large maguey behind them. That documented description adds an identification to the visible interlocking forms; it does not assign the figures an unverified narrative identity.

regions.question: What do you notice first in the vignette: the upright centre or the long points?

regions.label: Long points extend from the centre
regions.summary: Several slender points reach outward from the central form.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Several slender points reach outward from the central form. They narrow into sharp ends and contrast with the more rounded upright contours.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The outward points enlarge the illustration’s reach without filling its bounding area. They can make a small image feel more active than its size suggests.

regions.question: How would the vignette change if the points ended bluntly?

regions.label: A warm italic title
regions.summary: Pedro Páramo appears in orange italic lettering near the top.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Pedro Páramo appears in orange italic lettering near the top. The line is larger than the black author name beneath it.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The warm accent gives the title priority within a mostly quiet palette. The slant of the letters also introduces movement before the sharper vignette below.

regions.question: What does the orange contribute that a larger black title might not?

regions.label: A compact author credit
regions.summary: The small word por sits above Juan Rulfo in dark capitals.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The small word por sits above Juan Rulfo in dark capitals. Both lines are centred under the wider orange title.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: A compact credit leaves a large pause before the illustration. This spacing separates the act of naming the author from the less immediately legible image.

sections.heading: A small word assigns authorship
sections.body: The Spanish por introduces Juan Rulfo as the writer. Its modest size keeps the name and role readable without competing with the orange title above.

regions.question: How much of the hierarchy depends on size, and how much on the surrounding paper?

regions.label: A double rule contains the page
regions.summary: Two fine rectangular rules enclose the central design.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Two fine rectangular rules enclose the central design. The lines sit close together and follow the jacket’s slightly uneven photographed surface.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The double frame creates order around an image of irregular curves and points. Its restraint lets a small change of colour or shape become noticeable.

regions.question: Why might two fine lines feel different from one heavy border?

regions.label: A quiet line divides two zones
regions.summary: A thin horizontal rule runs across the framed area below the author.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A thin horizontal rule runs across the framed area below the author. It separates the compact title block from the broad paper around the vignette.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The rule gives the page a simple two-part organisation without adding another image. Its lightness keeps the lower area open rather than boxed into a dense panel.

regions.question: Does this divider feel like a pause or a barrier?

regions.label: The title’s colour returns below
regions.summary: The small italic Letras Mexicanas line appears below the illustration in a warm orange similar to the title.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The small italic Letras Mexicanas line appears below the illustration in a warm orange similar to the title. It is much narrower and lighter in emphasis.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: Repeating the accent connects the top and foot of the layout. The smaller line can be read as supporting information while remaining part of the same colour system.

regions.question: How does the return of orange affect your movement down the page?

regions.label: A publisher inside the lower rule
regions.summary: Fondo de Cultura Económica is printed in small dark capitals near the bottom of the framed area.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Fondo de Cultura Económica is printed in small dark capitals near the bottom of the framed area. The long line balances the shorter series name above.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The footer completes the structure with information about the publisher. Its close relationship to the rule makes it feel anchored after the floating vignette.

sections.heading: A novel in a named series
sections.body: The foundation identifies the 1955 first edition as Letras Mexicanas number 19, published by Fondo de Cultura Económica. The series and publisher wording on the jacket place the individual novel within that publishing programme.

regions.question: What makes this small footer feel more fixed than the central image?

regions.label: Paper makes the small image matter
regions.summary: A broad unprinted interval separates the horizontal rule from the top of the vignette.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A broad unprinted interval separates the horizontal rule from the top of the vignette. The paper shows uneven tone and subtle physical marks.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The pause gives the illustration room to operate at a modest scale. Adding more imagery here would reduce the force of the lone vignette.

regions.question: Would the same illustration feel as important in a densely filled cover?

regions.label: The copy has its own material history
regions.summary: The photographed left edge shows wear, colour change and the boundary of the physical book.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The photographed left edge shows wear, colour change and the boundary of the physical book. These marks differ from the regular printed frame.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: Wear belongs to this surviving copy, not necessarily to the original design. Recognising that distinction prevents accidental readings of damage as deliberate decoration.

regions.question: Which marks seem printed, and which seem to come from use or ageing?

connections.label: A restrained frame
connections.title: Curves inside rules
connections.text: The pointed vignette interrupts the quiet rectangle of the ruled layout.

connections.label: Two orange voices
connections.title: Title and series
connections.text: The title’s warm orange returns in the smaller italic series line.
